title: DialogBank, gold-standard ISO 24617-2 annotations (Bunt, Petukhova, Malchanau, Fang and Wijnhoven, LREC 2016; Language Resources and Evaluation 2019), its English dialogues in DiAML
held: DialogBank's pages state no licence, and its dialogues come from corpora with terms of their own (Switchboard, HCRC Map Task, TRAINS, DBOX, the Hujiang lessons). Its files are pinned; no word of them is committed, only how many acts they gave and their SHA-256. No gate downloads them, so nothing here is enforced where the Prism is built: the source is read only with --fetch, and test/oracle/intent.test.mjs reads it only when DIALOGUE_HELD names the acts tools/oracle/gen.py --fetch --held wrote, and says so when it does not.

unenforced.why: what each task-dimension act asks (the general-purpose functions mapped under acts); measured where the acts are supplied, never where the Prism is built, since no gate may download them
which words make a functional segment; the Prism reads one prompt as one segment
which earlier act an answer, an acceptance or a refusal responds to (ISO 24617-2 functional dependence relations); the Prism reads each line on its own and has no reader of what a turn depends on
which earlier acts a feedback act reports on (ISO 24617-2 feedback dependence relations); the Prism has no reader of feedback

the eight dimensions beside task (auto- and allo-feedback, turn, time, discourse structuring, own and partner communication, social obligations, contact management); the intent reader has a head for autoFeedback only, fit on AMI's Backchannel acts and held there (QR-16), and measured here where the acts are supplied; social obligations management has no head: the published mapping of AMI's classes names none for it and these dialogues hold 16 such acts

acts that accept, decline or address a request, a suggestion or an offer are commissives or directives whose content is the act they depend on; without functional dependence the reader cannot say what is committed to, so they are not mapped onto an intent
certainty, conditionality and sentiment qualifiers; the Prism reads none
rhetorical relations between acts (ISO 24617-8 core relations); the Prism reads none

comment: What each functional segment of a dialogue does, in every dimension, and which earlier acts it depends on, as ISO 24617-2's own editors annotated it. acts: the standard's general-purpose functions onto the router's intents, in the task dimension: the information-seeking functions a question, the information-providing functions a fact, the directives and the commissives that open an action (instruct, request, suggest, offer, promise) a task. malformed: files that are not well-formed XML as published (a <when> element left unclosed); they are pinned and not read, and nothing is repaired. unenforced: what the annotation carries that no reader of the Prism is yet held to, each with why; test/oracle/intent.test.mjs counts each where the acts are supplied. measured: what the intent reader found on the acts, when and where; a measurement, not a threshold any gate holds.

measured.where: a local build, not a gate
